name: HubSpot
tagline: A free CRM with marketing, sales and service hubs attached
description: HubSpot bundles a free CRM with paid marketing, sales and service hubs, adding AI writing, lead scoring and reporting that small teams can grow into over time.
priceNote: Free tier available; the Starter hub is $20 per seat/month on monthly billing ($7 per seat/month on annual billing for new customers); Professional is $890/month with a one-time $3,000 onboarding fee and Enterprise is quoted. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Small sales and marketing teams that want one CRM with marketing built in
pros: The free tier carries a usable CRM with contacts, deals and pipelines at no cost
Marketing, sales and service data sit on one record, so the handoff stops losing context
HubSpot AI drafts emails, logs calls and summarises meetings instead of making you type them
A large integration and template ecosystem connects a small stack without custom work
cons: Professional tier onboarding adds a $3,000 one-time fee that catches small buyers off guard
Credit-based limits on paid hubs make monthly forecasting harder than a flat seat price
The product is deep enough that a new admin loses weeks to setup before the first campaign
Buying Marketing Hub alone costs more than a focused email tool for the same list size

features.name: Free CRM
features.detail: Contacts, deals, pipelines and tasks for a small sales team

features.name: Marketing hub
features.detail: Email, landing pages, forms and workflows with A/B testing

features.name: HubSpot AI
features.detail: Email drafting, call logging, meeting summaries and content generation

features.name: Sales and service hubs
features.detail: Sequences, proposals, tickets and a knowledge base on one record

features.name: Analytics and attribution
features.detail: Funnels, campaign ROI and closed-lost reporting

features.name: Integrations and API
features.detail: Marketplace, webhooks and an open API for the rest of your stack

useCases: Start a startup pipeline on the free CRM and upgrade only when volume justifies it
Turn blog and newsletter traffic into a tracked lead funnel without extra tools
Give a small agency one place to manage client campaigns, contacts and monthly reporting
Trigger onboarding emails and support tickets the moment a deal closes
bestForWho: Growing SMB sales and marketing teams that want a genuine CRM with marketing automation attached to it.
verdict: HubSpot earns its reputation with the free tier, which is a real CRM rather than a demo, and that is how most small teams end up paying for it later. Once a lead arrives, the marketing, sales and service hubs share one record, so the context that used to live in three spreadsheets finally travels with the customer. The AI features are a genuine time saver on the busywork: call logging, meeting notes and first-draft emails. The honest warning is the jump to Professional, because the $3,000 onboarding fee and $890 monthly price land on a company that bought the free tier expecting a small bill. Teams that stay on Starter and treat it as a small-business CRM get excellent value.
